messages:
zoe: Quick non-work poll — what’s more likely to break your heart: a stray tab in YAML or an off-by-one in semver? :broken_heart:

kai: YAML tabs. Always. They sneak in like houseguests. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

maria: semver drama is theatrical though — major bump and suddenly everything's in therapy. 

zoe: ok but picture this: you merge a tiny config change and CI throws a 500 because of a tab. Game over.

kai: true. Also, can we make a new compiler pickup line? I got one: "Are you a linker? Because my symbols resolve when I'm around you." :sweat_smile:

maria: lol that’s terrible and I love it. Mine: "Call me a compiler, I'll optimize your loops out of existence." :laughing:

zoe: i'm saving both. Also dropping a cursed snippet for the group to fix: 
```yaml
service:
  name: inference
  replicas: 3
  resources:
	cpu: 2  # oops tab here
  memory: 8Gi
```

kai: (reacts with :facepalm:) that tab will haunt someone's Friday.

maria: pro tip: .editorconfig + pre-commit hook. and a pragmatic sed incantation: `git diff --check` before merge.

zoe: @kai you should write a tiny bot that comments "YAML ghosts detected" on PRs. call it yaml-therapy-bot.

build-bot: automated message: linter found 1 indentation error in config/service.yaml at line 5. See https://ci.redwood/inference/12345 

kai: omg build-bot just delivered the intervention. :clap:

maria: bonus points if yaml-therapy-bot responds with a Yoda quote: "Indentation, the path to the dark side is."

zoe: vote results: tabs win in chaos, semver wins in melodrama. Thread closed. :tada:
